# Active User

Meta description: An active user is a person who performs a meaningful action in an app within a set period. How DAU, WAU and MAU are measured.
Slug: active-user
Alt text: Table comparing DAU, WAU and MAU definitions
Category: Engagement

An active user is any person who completes at least one meaningful action inside an app during a defined window, such as a day, week, or month. Each product sets its own definition of a meaningful action.

## Why Active Users Matter

Tracking active users tells a product team whether growth is real usage or only installs. It also anchors retention math: a churned user is one who stops being active, so the active-user definition decides what churn means.

## Active User Metrics

| Metric | Window | Formula | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| DAU | 24 hours | Unique users with at least one qualifying action per day | Daily-habit products such as chat and fitness |
| WAU | 7 days | Unique users with at least one qualifying action per week | Weekly-cadence products |
| MAU | 30 days | Unique users with at least one qualifying action per month | Board reporting and pricing tiers |

A worked example: 2,000 DAU divided by 8,000 MAU gives a stickiness ratio of 25%, meaning a quarter of monthly users show up on a given day.

## Active Users and social.plus

social.plus reports active users per community feature, so a team can see whether chat, feeds, or live streams drive the daily action rather than reading one blended number.

## Key Takeaways

- An active user completes a meaningful action within a set window.
- DAU divided by MAU is the stickiness ratio and shows habit strength.
- Define the meaningful action once and keep it stable so trends stay comparable.
